relations.myth: God sends Raziel to convey a sacred book to Adam
relations.note: God commissions Raziel to transmit heavenly secrets and sacred knowledge to Adam.

relations.myth: Raziel transmits divine authority through the book
relations.note: Raziel acts as God’s messenger, while the book’s authority derives from God.

relations.myth: Jealous angels steal Adam’s book and cast it into sea
relations.note: Unnamed angels oppose the revelation Raziel gave Adam by stealing and discarding its book.

relations.myth: Rahab retrieves Raziel’s book from the sea
relations.note: At God’s command, Rahab recovers the discarded book originally delivered by Raziel.

relations.myth: Raphael replaces Raziel as Noah’s revealer
relations.note: A variant anthology stratum assigns Raphael, rather than Raziel, the revelation of sacred knowledge to Noah.

relations.myth: Hadarniel warns Adam within the secret-book narrative
relations.note: Hadarniel participates indirectly in the Adam-book complex without a personal meeting with Raziel.
Older compilations equate Raziel with Akraziel through similar offices and exegetical wordplay.
Older compilations equate Raziel with Gallizur through similar revelatory functions and wordplay.

relations.myth: Raziel creates or empowers the Nephilim with his blood
relations.note: In Shadowhunters fiction, Raziel creates or empowers the Nephilim by giving them his blood.
